**Triage Summary:**

Both findings are the same CVE (CVE-2022-29155) affecting two related OpenLDAP packages (libldap-2.4-2 and libldap-common) at version 2.4.44+dfsg-5+deb9u8. The vulnerability is rated CRITICAL with a 0.699 EPSS score and a fix is available, though it is not yet listed in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. This is a single issue requiring one remediation action rather than two separate problems.

**Recommended Action:** Upgrade both libldap packages to the patched version immediately. Verify the fix availability in your Debian 9 repository or backport channel, then deploy the update across affected systems. Document the upgrade completion and re-scan to confirm remediation.
review_summary:
# Triage Summary

This build contains **20 findings across 5 distinct vulnerability clusters**, all in outdated Debian 9 packages with no available patches. The critical OpenSSL issues (CVE-2022-2068, CVE-2022-1292, CVE-2022-2274) represent the highest risk—two are unfixable in this version, though CVE-2022-1292 has a patch available. The remaining findings span legacy libraries (bzip2, Python 2.7, SQLite, Berkeley DB) with low-to-moderate exploitability scores and no fixes, plus two npm dependencies (qs, decode-uri-component) with available patches. The root cause is the use of Debian 9 (EOL since 2020), which receives no security updates.

**Recommended Action:** Reject this build and require upgrade to a current Debian LTS version (11 or 12). If immediate deployment is unavoidable, apply patches to CVE-2022-1292 and the npm dependencies, document the unfixable OpenSSL/legacy library risks, and implement compensating controls (network segmentation, WAF rules). Do not merge without explicit risk acceptance from security leadership.
